title: Propagating context across services, queues and scheduled jobs

videos.script: Four processes, and one trace. The storefront, orders, payments and the mailer each run alone, in their own memory. {{four}} So how did payments know which trace it belonged to? Something travelled with the request. A header, fifty-five characters long. {{header}} In this lesson you read that header straight out of the database, and take it apart. You see the two calls that write it and read it. Then you delete one of them, and watch payments fall out of the trace without a single error. {{break}} The same header crosses the queue, inside the message. You stop the mailer, and the trace waits twenty seconds for it. {{queue}} And the nightly report, which nobody calls, gets a trace of its own, with links to every order it counted. {{report}}
